Issued at 413 AM EST Wed Nov 4 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

120kt sub-tropical jet stretches from SoCal into the Lower MS Valley 
hitting a wall of ridging over the eastern US...resulting in flow 
sharpening from SW-NE to S-N over the Mid MS Valley up into the 
Upper Midwest. A bit of an omega block appearing in the 
western/central US...with MS Valley energy as the downstream lobe of 
troughing...and energy trudging into NV as the upstream lobe 
(current signals it should continue its eastward trudgery)...with 
ridge centered over MT. Zonal polar jet across northern Canada 
keeping things in motion across north/central Canada...resulting in 
a PV strand from the Northern Plains up into Quebec and 
strengthening deformation on the northern side of the system 
(evident in satellite imagery). Plume of Gulf moisture right up the 
MS Valley into the Upper Great Lakes...with pwat values of 1.42in at 
0z here, and 1.66in at GRB (approx 4-5 standard deviations above the 
climo mean). On satellite, you can see the moisture spreading out 
along the deformation axis across northern MN/southern 
Ontario...rather a stereotypical comma head, with convection from IL 
to LA along the cold front/dry slot (and where there is more 
instability to play with)...and a bit of a break in the action from 
WI into Lower MI in the warm sector of this system. 850mb temps at 
or above 12C over MI attm, with a bit of 0C air trying to hang on 
over the Dakotas with the cold conveyor belt of this system. Almost 
due south 50kt LLJ over IL poking up into Lake MI attm, though 
little in the way of temperature or moisture advection taking place 
into northern MI attm. Maturing surface cyclone over the Upper MS 
Valley...and 1021mb surface high over the Prairies oozing into the 
northern Plains in the wake of this low, helping keep the pressure 
gradient strong on the backside of this system as well. 

PV maxima to lift northward toward the area this morning, dragging 
some showers through from south to north; front swings north through 
the area this afternoon into tonight as the parent surface low 
continues to wind up to our west. This should bring some more 
showers to the area going into this evening and the overnight. It 
will cool off later tonight into Thursday, with little in the way of 
a diurnal temp swing expected as cold air will be rushing into the 
region, especially late Thursday into Thursday night as a lobe of 
northern stream energy digs into the trough for the end of the work 
week...with breezy north winds and lake effect rain (snow?) showers. 
Guidance is going back to the idea of troughing getting cut off in 
our region for the end of the week/weekend, which has potential to 
keep things unsettled and most likely fall like, though it's 
possible some ridging may try to sneak in Saturday/Saturday night 
ahead of a northern stream niblet. Still unclear whether this 
feature will also dig into the Great Lakes or remain just to our 
north. Overall...appears the northern stream will remain progressive 
and active into the early part of next week; sort of a clipper-y 
idea with prevailing NW to WNW flow aloft. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Rain (storms?) today...Expect first dry slot to lift through this 
morning/early afternoon which should lead to convective instability 
     and potential for an uptick in shower activity this morning from 
southwest to northeast. Perhaps even a rumble of thunder? Better 
chance of that would be later this afternoon ahead of the cold front 
swinging northward across the area. Expect a bit more potent low-
level lift with this feature, given signals for strong low-level 
fgen and perhaps a few dozen joules of low-level cape. Can't help 
but wonder if we could get some low-topped shenanigans as the cold 
front blows through this afternoon, as deep layer (and even low-
level) shear will be mediocre/marginal, around 20-30kts. Could be 
something to keep an eye on. Think the best shot at this would be 
near and east of I-75 where there is a better likelihood of some 
directional shear ahead of the front with southeasterly surface 
winds. With pwats still above average as this system exits...any 
storms could produce some locally heavier rainfall totals, but these 
should also be relatively quick-moving...though there could be 
something of a pivot point near the Tip of the Mitt/M-68 corridor. 

Breezy for EUP Late Thursday into Friday...currently looking at 
potential for a strong pressure gradient on the backside of the 
departing low Thursday afternoon/night...which looks strongest 
across the EUP and Lake Superior attm. Pressure gradient appears to 
support sustained winds in the realm of 15-20kts from the N/NE 
(likely 20-25kts or better over Lake Superior into Whitefish Bay).
